prop:alpha-em-categorical-trace-ratio:
Proposition Algebraic identity: \alpha_{EM} = h^2 / [q \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})]. Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] be the base ring. Let h = q - q^{-1} denote the skein parameter. Let T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} be the two genus-4-saturating torus knots ((T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}) is the unique pair of genus-4 torus knots). Let \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q denote the top-channel decoration of a torus knot (Top-channel decoration \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} of a torus knot). The bare electromagnetic fine-structure constant 1/\alpha_{EM} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q (Electromagnetic coupling from the antisymmetric braiding and force-carrier crossings) admits the categorical-trace-ratio decomposition:

  \boxed{\;\;
    \alpha_{EM}
    \;=\;
    \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})}
  \;\;}

Derivation

By Top-channel decoration \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} of a torus knot, \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{m,p}) = q^{w} - q^{-w} with w = (m-1)p, the bar-odd part of the eigenvalue q^{w} by which the braid (\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{m-1})^{p} acts in the trivial representation of H_m(q). Both knots here are presented on their braid index (2 \le 9 and 3 \le 5).

For T_{2,9}, w = 9, so \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) = q^{9} - q^{-9} = h\,[9]_q. For 2-strand knots this agrees with the sum of the two Hecke characters, q^{9} + (-q^{-1})^{9}.

For T_{3,5}, w = 10, so \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5}) = q^{10} - q^{-10} = h\,[10]_q. Here the sum of the three characters on V_{(3)}, V_{(2,1)}, V_{(1,1,1)} would instead give q^{10} - 1 + q^{-10}, because \chi_{(2,1)}((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^{5}) = -1; the identity uses the top-channel value, not that sum.

Substitution produces the result:

  \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9}) \cdot \delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})}
  \;=\;
  \frac{h^{2}}{q \cdot h\,[9]_q \cdot h\,[10]_q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q}
  \;=\;
  \alpha_{EM}.

\square

Numerical verification

The algebraic identity holds over R at every invertible q with h = q - q^{-1} invertible. Evaluating both sides at the proton-pinned aether parameter q_0 = 1.1099785828\ldots reproduces \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} = 1/(q_0\,[9]_{q_0}\,[10]_{q_0}) = 7.30870156 \times 10^{-3} (q_0\,[9]_{q_0}\,[10]_{q_0} = 136.823209), in exact agreement with Electromagnetic coupling from the antisymmetric braiding and force-carrier crossings. Conjecture Computational-time identification: the binding Borel variable is the loop proper time. Let s denote the Schwinger proper-time variable of the \zeta-regularized one-loop photon determinant on the Bring Jacobian, whose loop expansion weighs proper time by the scale-invariant measure \varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s} with unit \varsigma. Let N(n) denote the binding normalizer forced by the normalization bridge — the unique strip N(n) = (n-1)! making the binding generating function the carrier of the proved depth-2 confluent kernel (the normalization leg of The q-difference kernel R is the jet-prolongation symbol, carried by the binding q-lift module).

The framework premises are named:

  • P1 (scale-freedom): the aether is scale-free; the locally realized modulus q_0 is local data, not a structural scale of the aether.
  • P2 (computational time): proper time is computational time — s counts the aether's computation steps.

Statement. The binding sector's Borel variable and the loop's Schwinger proper time s are the same aether object. Under P2 both are the aether's computational time, and the identification takes the quantitative form: the normalizer is the n-th moment of the loop's proper-time measure,

N(n) \;=\; \int_0^\infty s^{\,n}\, e^{-s}\,\varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s} \;=\; \varsigma\,(n-1)! .

Conditional consequences. Both are conditional on this conjecture (together with P1/P2 where noted); neither is a derivation of it.

  1. The unit is forced: \varsigma = 1. The proved identity n \cdot N(n) = n! rescales under a unit \varsigma to \varsigma \cdot n! = n!, so \varsigma = 1 exactly; the rival value \varsigma = \tfrac12 gives n!/2 \neq n! (an exact distinguisher, proved unconditionally). Conditionally, this fixes the unit — one nat per proper-time e-fold, with k_B = 1 so that entropy is counted in nats.
  2. The \tfrac12 is located per-channel bar-even. With total unit \varsigma = 1, the working per-channel coefficient \tfrac12\,a_0 = 1/(8\pi) — where a_0 = 1/(4\pi) is the derived two-dimensional heat-kernel unit entering the \alpha_{EM} insertion (\alpha_{EM} as the root of the self-consistent fixed-point cubic) — arises from the doubled-pair channel split. This tips the \tfrac12-adjudication toward the \rho-split reading (total unit one, the \tfrac12 in the channel split) and against the energy-Jacobian reading (\varsigma = \tfrac12 on the proper-time side), which would break the moment identity.

The identification is a dictionary premise between two sectors — the \alpha_{EM} loop measure and the binding q-Borel transform. It is stated here as a precise, falsifiable structural claim: a derivation would fix the unit; a refutation would rule the identification out. The two sectors would share one unit, and the binding side's is forced by a proved identity; the checkable content is the moment identity above, verified exactly at orders n = 1 through 6.

At the fibre level (q \neq 1) the identification is consistent only in the balanced q-Borel convention: the one-sided normalizer [n-1]_q! is bar-covariant with exact weight q^{-(n-1)(n-2)/2}, so it cannot equal a bar-invariant proper-time object, while the balanced normalizer q^{-(n-1)(n-2)/4}\,[n-1]_q! is exactly bar-invariant with vanishing first-order q-correction. The conjecture's representability content is therefore a claim about a canonical choice of integral representation for a formally performed operation, and under that reformulation its two levels separate into distinct problems.

def:schwinger-measure-unit:
Definition Schwinger proper-time measure and its unit \varsigma. The Schwinger proper-time measure with unit \varsigma is the scale-invariant density on the proper-time half-line,

\mu_\varsigma \;=\; \varsigma\,\frac{ds}{s}, \qquad s \in (0, \infty),

where s is the Schwinger proper-time variable of the one-loop determinant and the scalar \varsigma is the Schwinger measure unit. The shape is rigid: a density f satisfying the scale-invariance functional equation f(\lambda s)\,\lambda = f(s) equals f(1)/s, so \mu_\varsigma is the unique scale-invariant choice up to the single scalar \varsigma.

The canonical unit is \varsigma = 1: in the logarithmic coordinate the measure of one e-fold [s, e\,s] is exactly \varsigma, and with k_B = 1 (entropy in nats) the unit is denominated in nats per proper-time e-fold. Downstream consumers reference this result for the per-loop measure normalization; under the canonical unit and the per-channel \tfrac12 split, the working per-channel coefficient is \tfrac12 \cdot \frac{1}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{8\pi}.

Conjectural backing of canonicity. Defining \mu_1 names a construction; the canonicity of the choice \varsigma = 1 is not proved. It is conditionally forced by the computational-time identification Computational-time identification: the binding Borel variable is the loop proper time, through the moment identity n \cdot N(n) = n! for the binding normalizer N(n), and, separately, by the framework premises P1 (aether scale-freedom) and P2 (proper time as computational time) stated there. Unconditionally it remains a unit convention of the same species the framework canonizes elsewhere for discrete time steps. Empirical support is exact rather than numerical: the unit-measure moment identity holds at orders 1 through 6, and a pin-invariance falsifier eliminates every intrinsic per-step rival unit.

Remark Schrödinger's color metric, diminishing returns, and a falsifiable q_0 prediction. The categorical q-chromaticity construction yields a falsifiable prediction regarding human color perception. The empirical result (Bujack et al., 2022).

Bujack et al. [bujack2022] report experimental evidence that perceived color differences violate Riemannian additivity along geodesics. The observed differences satisfy the strict inequality:

  \Delta E(A, B) + \Delta E(B, C) > \Delta E(A, C).

This diminishing-returns principle contradicts the assumptions of Riemann, Helmholtz, and Schrödinger [schrodinger1920color]. A crowdsourced color-triad experiment (75{,}896 training trials across ten splits, R^2 = 0.556, F(3, 60) = 25.00, p < 0.001) yielded a negative average-difference coefficient (\beta_{\bar d} = -0.005, t(60) = -5.566, p < 0.001) [bujack2022, Results, Table 1]. (18)], the logarithmic model f_{\log}(\Delta\psi) = b\log(a\Delta\psi + 1)/\log(a + 1) matched the flexible monotonic spline in predictive accuracy, leading Bujack et al. to propose a second-order Weber–Fechner law in which perceived differences grow logarithmically at large stimulus separations [bujack2022, Discussion]. Prior psychophysical studies fit perceived color differences to a power law with an exponent near 0.5.

prop:integer-stability:
Proposition Integer stability: the valley of stability as a Diophantine constraint. Physical nuclei require integer proton and neutron numbers. Stable hadrons correspond to integer solutions of a quadratic energy minimisation. The continuous optimum p^*(A) defines the beta-stability line.

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes universe with aether parameter q. At a fixed mass number A = Z + N, the nuclear binding energy is a strictly convex quadratic in the proton number p:

  E(p, A) = 
  \underbrace{\left(\frac{a_C}{A^{1/3}} + \frac{4a_A}{A}\right)}_{\alpha(A)} p^2
  - \underbrace{4a_A}_{\gamma} p
  + \delta(A),

where a_C = \lambda_C is the Coulomb coefficient and a_A = a_{\mathrm{asym}} the Pauli asymmetry coefficient of beta stability, the p-dependent part is that of a_C\,p^2/A^{1/3} + a_A (A - 2p)^2/A, and \delta(A) collects terms independent of p.

The continuous minimum is

  p^*(A) =  \frac{\gamma}{2\alpha(A)} =  \frac{A}{2 + \dfrac{a_C}{2a_A} A^{2/3}}.

Because E is strictly convex in p, the exact integer minimiser p_{\mathrm{stab}}(A) is one of the two nearest integers to the continuous minimum:

  p_{\mathrm{stab}}(A) = \mathrm{argmin}_{p \in \{0, 1, \ldots, A\}} E(p, A) \in \bigl\{\lfloor p^*(A) \rfloor, \lceil p^*(A) \rceil\bigr\}.

Archimedean specialisation. The binding energy E(p), its continuous optimum p^*, and the convex-minimisation argument are stated over \mathbb{R}. The integer-minimiser bound relies on the real ordering.

  t^3 =  p(2 + ct^2),

Setup. A nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) is a satellite link of A = Z + N Borromean components. Its braid word in B_{3A} reduces to a unique Gröbner–Shirshov normal form \mathcal{N}(Z, N) in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_{3A}(q).

Each nucleon is a Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3(q_1, q_2, q_3) with quark strands:

  • Proton: \mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d})
  • Neutron: \mathfrak{n} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d})

The crossing type at each generator \sigma_i depends on the quark flavours of the two strands. The \mathfrak{u}\text{-}\mathfrak{u} crossing is positive. The \mathfrak{d}\text{-}\mathfrak{d} crossing is negative. The \mathfrak{u}\text{-}\mathfrak{d} crossing is mixed.

The T_{3,5} weak vertex

The weak interaction is mediated by the torus knot T_{3,5}. Its braid word in B_3 is:

  \beta_{T_{3,5}} =  (\sigma_1 \sigma_2)^5

This word has 10 crossings. In the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_3(q), the Hecke reduction of (\sigma_1 \sigma_2)^5 eliminates squares via T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1. This produces a polynomial in the reduced basis of H_3(q). The Markov trace of this polynomial is the weak vertex form factor:

  \mathcal{W}(q)
   := 
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\bigl((\sigma_1 \sigma_2)^5\bigr)
   \in  \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]

The single-crossing Skein amplitude s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} appears as the coupling at each crossing of the T_{3,5} braid. The full vertex factor is the Markov trace \mathcal{W}(q) of all 10 crossings, not s^2.

The T_{3,5} braid insertion introduces 10 crossings into the nuclear braid word. Gröbner–Shirshov reduction resolves these crossings into three components:

Crossings Destination Structure
3 Electron e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (closure: Hopf link) 3 positive crossings, a braid factor of the vertex
0 Antineutrino K_{0_1}^{\sigma} (mirror unknot) Trivial topology

The 7 re-reduction crossings change the R2 step count between parent and daughter normal forms. This dominates the Q-value. The single-crossing approximation misses 6 of these 7 crossings.

Crossing partition and the Skein relation

Gröbner–Shirshov reduction partitions the 10 crossings of T_{3,5}. The electron word takes 3. The neutrino unknot takes 0. The daughter nuclear braid absorbs the remaining 7 as R2 moves.

The Skein relation acts at each of the 10 crossings:

  q  [L_+] -  q^{-1} [L_-]
  =  (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})  [L_0]

The transition amplitude depends on the accumulated effect of 10 such relations, not 1.

The involution q \mapsto q^{-1} on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra relates \beta^- and \beta^+. It acts as:

  \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q)
  = \frac{q \mu_a + q^{-1} \mu_b}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}
  \xrightarrow{q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}} 
  \mathcal{S}_{ba}(q)
  = \frac{q \mu_b + q^{-1} \mu_a}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}

These are distinct when \mu_a \neq \mu_b. The asymmetry \mathcal{S}_{ab} - \mathcal{S}_{ba} = (q - q^{-1})(\mu_a - \mu_b)/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}) is the weak asymmetry. This drives the Q-value.

Note that the pair-Skein expression above uses the bar-symmetric denominator q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2} rather than the reciprocal of the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1): the symmetry \mathcal{S}_{ba}(q) = \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q^{-1}) relies on the q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} invariance of q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}, which z = q^3/(q^2+1) does not satisfy. Gröbner–Shirshov reduction decomposes the T_{3,5} braid (\sigma_1 \sigma_2)^5 into the lepton pair and a reduction residue. In the generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1 the vertex is (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5, and the electron word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (electron) is a braid factor of it:

  (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5 = e^- \cdot \bigl(e^- \cdot (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\bigr)

The proof is the braid relation once: e^- \cdot e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^3, the full twist. So the electron accounts for 3 of the 10 crossings as an identity of braids, not only as a count. The antineutrino unknot K_{0_1} accounts for 0. The remaining 7 crossings, e^- \cdot (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2, are the weak vertex residue. They are absorbed into R2 moves during re-reduction. The mirror vertex factors the same way through the positron: (\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1})^5 = e^+ \cdot \bigl(e^+ \cdot (\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1})^2\bigr).

  L_0^{-} =  e^- \sqcup T_{1,0}^{\sigma}
  \qquad (\beta^- \text{ decay: } e^- + \nu_e^{\sigma})
  L_0^{+} =  e^+ \sqcup T_{1,0}
  \qquad (\beta^+ \text{ decay: } e^+ + \nu_e)

The Q-value (10-crossing)

The transition energy is the difference in categorical actions between parent and daughter. It accounts for all 10 crossings of the T_{3,5} insertion:

  Q
  = 
  \mathfrak{S}_q[\mathcal{N}(Z, N)]
  - 
  \mathfrak{S}_q[\mathcal{N}(Z \pm 1, N \mp 1)]
  - 
  m_e

The parent and daughter normal forms differ at all crossings affected by the T_{3,5} insertion and its re-reduction. The 7 re-reduction crossings from the weak vertex residue modify inter-nucleon crossing types at the converting quark's strand. They change \binom{A-1}{1} \cdot 3 inter-nucleon crossings.

  1. Extract the 3-crossing electron word e^-, a braid factor of the vertex.
  2. Reduce the remaining 7 crossings via R2 moves (T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1) and R3/far-commutativity moves.
  3. Propagate the flavour change through all inter-nucleon crossings involving the converting quark's strand.

  Q =  \Delta(\text{R2 steps})
   \times  (q - q^{-1})
   \times  (\text{pair Skein scale})

Insufficiency of the single-crossing approximation

The previous single-crossing approximation captured only 1 of the 10 crossings in the weak vertex. This explains:

  1. Systematic overshoot. Predictions for heavy-nucleus half-lives overshoot by 10–17\%. The missing 9 crossings contribute phase space. Including them shortens the half-life.
  2. Tritium accuracy. The error for A = 3 is < 2\%. The nuclear braid is short. The 7 re-reduction crossings have limited room to propagate. The single-crossing approximation succeeds accidentally.
  3. Mass-dependent correction. Heavier nuclei have more inter-nucleon crossings affected by the flavour change. The 7 re-reduction crossings modify more transfer matrices.

Open computation. The braid-level split 3 + 0 + 7 is the factorisation above. The weak vertex form factor is computed under the two-term trace in the half-life proof of this chapter: its one-term part is \mathcal{W}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5) = q^2(q^{12}+q^8-1)/(q^2+1)^2, and its connected part depends on the charges of the three vertex strands, which are not derived.
